speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing shortness of breath and a large ovarian mass. Do you have any history of weight loss, night sweats, or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the abdominal swelling feel heavy or painful, and have you noticed any early satiety or bloating after eating small meals? I also need to know if you have any family history of breast or ovarian cancer.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass, ascites causing increased abdominal girth, and shortness of breath likely due to pleural effusion, this presentation is classic for Meigs' syndrome. I will confirm this with imaging and tumor markers. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT, REQUEST TEST: CA-125, REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present. CA-125: Level Normal. Chest X-Ray: Right-sided pleural effusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of an ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with a normal CA-125 level is highly suggestive of a benign fibroma. This clinical triad is known as Meigs' syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs' syndrome
